title: Artificial Neural Network Model for Forecasting Distributed Photovoltaic Generation
content: Most micro- and small-scale distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems operate behind the meter, making their generation not directly observable by the power grid, as part of the electricity produced is consumed locally. This paper investigates a methodology for estimating hourly PV generation profiles using artificial neural networks (ANNs) trained with publicly available generation data from centralized PV power plants monitored by the Brazilian National System Operator and meteorological records from the Brazilian National Institute of Meteorology. The proposed model uses 34 input variables derived from four nearby meteorological stations and the geographical coordinates of the location of interest to estimate generation normalized in per unit (p.u.). Three approaches were compared: individual ANN models, regionally generalized ANN models, and a linear irradiance-based reference model known as PESRC. For Pirapora, Lapa, and Dracena, the individual models achieved coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.87, 0.81, and 0.95, respectively, while the generalized ANNs obtained 0.83, 0.79, and 0.79. The generalized models outperformed PESRC in the first two cases, demonstrating the strong potential of ANNs to capture nonlinear relationships in photovoltaic generation time series.
